intro: The verb ser is used for identity and origin; the verb estar is used for location and temporary states. Today you learn to conjugate estar and use it in daily situations.
b1.texto:
In Spanish there are two verbs for «to be»:

- **Ser**: identity, profession, origin and regular traits (soy de Madrid, es profesor, Ana es alta).
- **Estar**: the location of someone or something, and temporary states (estoy en Madrid, está ocupado, estoy cansada).

To say that you are at home, use **en casa** (without an article): «estoy en casa». Saying «en la casa» refers to a specific physical building.

The present forms are: **estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están**. The written accent on **está** distinguishes the verb form from «esta» (feminine demonstrative).
b4.texto:
We use **estar** to point out where a person, building or object is, and also to express how we feel:

- The museum **está aquí**; the park **está allí**.
- Today **estamos cansados**, but tomorrow we will be fine.

Remember: origin takes ser («soy de Lima»), while temporary stay takes estar («estoy en Lima»).
b5.f0.texto: Pablo arrives home early in the afternoon.
b5.f1.texto: He is very tired after work.
b5.f2.texto: Lucía is in the living room and greets him with a smile.
b5.f3.texto: Ana is busy working in her room.
b5.f4.texto: She studies Spanish at her desk with great care and attention.
b5.f5.texto: All the flatmates are very happy living together in the flat.
b6.pregunta: Which sentence indicates origin («I am from Madrid»)?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: origin is always expressed using the verb ser.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: this indicates where you are right now (location).
b6.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: this describes a temporary physical state.
b7.pregunta: How do you ask where the museum is located?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: estar is used for the location of a place.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: «es» would define what it is, not where it is.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: «estoy» is the first person form («yo»).
b9.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I am at home».
p.estoy.consejo: First person of estar: «yo estoy bien».
p.estás.consejo: Second person singular. Written accent on the a: «¿dónde estás?».
p.está.consejo: Third person singular. Has an accent to differ from «esta».
p.estáis.consejo: Second person plural (Spain). Written accent on the a.
p.están.consejo: Third person plural: «ellos están en casa».
p.bien.consejo: Adverb indicating a good state: «estoy bien».
p.mal.consejo: Adverb opposite to bien: «hoy me siento mal».
p.en casa.consejo: Usual set phrase with no article: «estoy en casa».
p.aquí.consejo: Close to the speaker: «estamos aquí». Has an accent.
p.allí.consejo: Far from the speaker: «Ana está allí». Has an accent.
p.nosotros.consejo: A group «we» that includes yourself. Stress on «SO»: no-SO-tros. For an all-female group, use «nosotras».
p.habitación.consejo: Words ending in «-ción» carry a tilde on the «ó» and stress it: a-bi-ta-THYON. Think «habitar», to live in.
p.estudia.consejo: From «estudiar», to study. The stress falls on «TU», and the final «ia» glides into one syllable, «dya».
p.mucha.consejo: Feminine of «mucho». It matches «atención», a feminine noun, so it ends in «-a».
p.atención.consejo: It looks like English attention, but the tilde sits on the «ó» and the stress lands there: a-ten-THYON.
p.compañeros.consejo: Plural of «compañero». The «ñ» sounds like the «ny» in canyon, so say kom-pa-NYE-ros.
p.contentos.consejo: From «contento», pleased. Notice it starts with «con», like the English word content, but the stress is on «TEN».
